approachQuestion.prompt:
Surveyed courtyard area

A simple polygon is given by its n boundary vertices in cyclic order, either clockwise or counterclockwise. Return twice its geometric area as a nonnegative integer. The first vertex is not repeated at the end.

Example 1: [(0,0),(4,0),(0,3)] -> 12.
Example 2: [(0,3),(4,0),(0,0)] -> 12.
Example 3: [(1,1),(3,1),(3,2),(1,2)] -> 4.

Constraints and assumptions: 3 <= n <= 200000. Coordinates are integers in [-100000,100000]. Polygon has nonzero area, no self-intersections and no consecutive repeated vertices. Do not reorder or copy vertices. Return only the doubled area. Choose the best time bound among the offered correct methods, then the least auxiliary storage when time ties.

options.text: Sum x[i]*y[j]-y[i]*x[j] for each edge, including last-to-first, and take the absolute value only after all contributions are added.
options.feedback: Signed contributions cancel overlaps and recover the polygon's oriented doubled area. Taking the final absolute value permits either traversal direction.

options.text: Compute the same n signed contributions into a new array, sum that array, then take the absolute value.
options.feedback: It obtains the correct signed sum but stores values needed only once; a running sum suffices.

options.text: Sum the absolute value of every edge contribution.
options.feedback: For the rectangle [(1,1),(3,1),(3,2),(1,2)] this gives 12 instead of 4 because signed cancellations are lost.

options.text: Sum signed contributions only for adjacent listed pairs and take the absolute value.
options.feedback: For [(1,1),(3,1),(3,2),(1,2)] it gives 5 instead of 4; the closing edge contributes -1.

feedback.reason: Accumulate signed boundary contributions including the closing edge.
details: Scan all n edges, including the last-to-first edge. Add x[i]*y[j]-y[i]*x[j] for j=(i+1) mod n, then return the absolute value of the total.

Include the closing last-to-first edge in the signed cross sum. Clockwise order changes its sign but not absolute doubled area. Taking absolute values edge by edge would lose cancellations required by the polygon formula.

“Sum x[i]*y[j]-y[i]*x[j] for each edge, including last-to-first, and take the absolute value only after all contributions are added.”: Signed contributions cancel overlaps and recover the polygon's oriented doubled area. Taking the final absolute value permits either traversal direction.

“Compute the same n signed contributions into a new array, sum that array, then take the absolute value.”: It obtains the correct signed sum but stores values needed only once; a running sum suffices.
“Sum the absolute value of every edge contribution.”: For the rectangle [(1,1),(3,1),(3,2),(1,2)] this gives 12 instead of 4 because signed cancellations are lost.
“Sum signed contributions only for adjacent listed pairs and take the absolute value.”: For [(1,1),(3,1),(3,2),(1,2)] it gives 5 instead of 4; the closing edge contributes -1.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (signed-boundary-sum). Let n be the number of vertices. Choose its tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
Include initialization and any copying; no hidden preprocessing or cache.

feedback.reason: One exact cross contribution per polygon edge uses one accumulator.
details: All n edges are visited once with constant arithmetic per edge, and every edge can affect the area. Only an index and signed accumulator are needed. Each cross term has magnitude at most 2*10^10; even the sum of absolute term bounds is at most 4*10^15 and fits signed 64-bit.
Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Correct: one complete cyclic scan and a scalar sum.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This would save edge contributions; the revealed method does not.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The method does not compare every pair of vertices.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The variable-length boundary must be scanned.
